name: Matal
catalog_citation: Verdizade, Allahverdi. 2018. Selected topics in the grammar and lexicon of Matal. MA thesis, Department of Linguistics, Stockholm University (DiVA diva2:1253306, via web.archive.org).
catalog_locator: sec. 3.2 (p. 17 of PDF), sec. 3.4 Orthography (pp. 19-20), sec. 4.2.x tense (p. 29); abstract p. i
catalog_quote: Tense is expressed either by altered tone in the stem vowel or morphologically. ... The same approach was applied in investigating indicated tone, that is, verb forms that have a vowel marked by the diacritical mark <◌̀>. Minimal pairs were found in identical verb forms, with indicated tone being the only contrastive feature. ... As far as accent marks on the vowels denoting letters are concerned, only grave accent marks are used in the Bible text, suggesting that it denotes the tone that is marked. It is common for Chadic languages to reflect tonal variation only partially or not at all in conventional writing. ... Generally, tense is associated with the marked tone denoting past tense/perfective in Matal. As mentioned in §4.2.1, marked tone is denoted by grave accent mark over the vowel. Present tense is unmarked.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: every segment of the deciding quotation and the example forms are verbatim in the Verdizade 2018 PDF we hold/txt at the stated sections/pages. The classification 'tonal, no word-stress rule stated' is faithful to that source. But the source is a 54-pp MA thesis on grammar/lexicon working from a partially tone-marked Bible text; its evidence for lexical tone is second-hand from Rossing 1978, which Glottolog lists as the only phonology covering Matal (408 pp) and which we do not hold. Gravina 2014 (downloaded now, open LOT PDF) has a Matal section but explicitly excludes tone and stress, so it is silent. Nothing seen suggests the tonal coding is wrong (Rossing's transcriptions as reproduced mark H/L tone on every vowel; Central Chadic neighbours Podoko, Mada etc. are tonal), so this is 'thin' rather than 'at-risk'. Action: obtain Rossing 1978 (ProQuest/ILL) and, if reachable

PDF p.20 (sec. 3.4); 'Generally, tense is associated with the marked tone.

sources.quote: Bibliographic record only; establishes that the only dedicated phonological description covering Matal is Rossing 1978 (not held). Other Glottolog items are comparative wordlists (Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994; de Colombel 1982), a 15-pp lexical-semantics paper (K'Ayyang Foba & Dougophe 2020) and ethnography (Lembezat 1950; Juillerat 1968-1981).

Rossing's Muktile chapter (around p.43) would state the tone system first-hand and show whether any stress/accent is described alongside tone, as in some neighbouring Central Chadic descriptions.
